title: Practice: Circle Films Transaction Analysis

slides.visual_text: Book page headed Transaction Analysis, with an accounting-equation table for each transaction (Assets = Liabilities + Equity). Transaction 1: After incorporating, Circle Films issues 3,000 shares of common stock to investors for ₹15,000 cash. Assets increase because cash of ₹15,000 is received; equity increases because investors contributed cash for an ownership interest, so common stock increases. Table: Cash prior 0, +₹15,000, new ₹15,000 = Liabilities ₹0 + Common Stock ₹15,000. Transaction 2: Circle Films purchases a video camera for ₹9,000 and memory cards for ₹1,000. One asset (cash) is exchanged for other assets (equipment and supplies); assets both increase and decrease by ₹10,000; no change in total assets. Table: Cash 15,000, -10,000, new 5,000; Supplies +1,000; Equipment +9,000; total assets ₹15,000 = ₹0 + ₹15,000. Transaction 3: Circle Films receives a ₹1,500 payment immediately after filming a customer's wedding. Cash is received, but the increase results from filming the wedding; an inflow of assets from providing a service is a revenue. Revenues increase net income and therefore retained earnings, so equity increases. Table: Cash 5,000 +1,500 = 6,500; Retained Earnings 0 +1,500 = 1,500; total assets ₹16,500 = ₹0 + ₹16,500. Page number 55, Chapter 3: Recording Accounting Transactions.

Transaction Analysis (Cont'd). Transaction 4: Circle Films receives a ₹2,000 deposit from a customer to film her parents' fiftieth wedding anniversary. Cash is received so assets increase, but it has not yet provided the service, so it has an obligation to the customer and liabilities increase. Table: Cash 6,500 +2,000 = 8,500; Unearned Revenue +2,000; total assets ₹18,500 = ₹2,000 + ₹16,500. Transaction 5: Circle Films paid ₹250 cash to run an ad in the local paper. Assets decrease; a decrease in assets from operating a business is an expense; expenses decrease net income and therefore retained earnings, so equity decreases. Table: Cash 8,500 -250 = 8,250; Retained Earnings 1,500 -250 = 1,250; total assets ₹18,250 = ₹2,000 + ₹16,250. Transaction 6: Circle Films films a dance competition, leaving a ₹3,500 invoice with the customer. Although no cash is received, not all accounting transactions affect cash; the firm now has a receivable, so assets increase, and because it is generated by providing a service the firm has additional revenues and more equity. Very similar to transaction 3, with the only difference being the type of asset that increases. Table: Accounts Receivable +3,500; Retained Earnings 1,250 +3,500 = 4,750; total assets ₹21,750 = ₹2,000 + ₹19,750. Page 56.

Transaction Analysis (Cont'd). Transaction 7: Circle Films purchases another ₹9,000 video camera by signing a nine-month promissory note requiring payment of principal and interest at maturity; interest is charged at a 6% annual rate. Like transaction 2 it receives equipment so assets increase, but it promises to pay cash and interest in nine months, so liabilities increase. Table: Equipment 9,000 +9,000 = 18,000; Notes Payable 0 +9,000 = 9,000; total assets ₹30,750 = ₹11,000 + ₹19,750. Transaction 8: Circle Films receives ₹3,500 from the customer in payment of the open invoice from transaction 6. One asset is exchanged for another: cash increases while receivables decrease; no change in total assets. Table: Cash 8,250 +3,500 = 11,750; Accounts Receivable 3,500 -3,500 = 0; total assets ₹30,750 = ₹11,000 + ₹19,750. Transaction 9: Circle Films pays wages of ₹2,000 to its employees. Cash decreases by ₹2,000 so assets decrease; the payment is an outflow from operating the business, an expense, which reduces equity. Table: Cash 11,750 -2,000 = 9,750; Retained Earnings 4,750 -2,000 = 2,750; total assets ₹28,750 = ₹11,000 + ₹17,750. Page 57.

Transaction Analysis (Cont'd). Transaction 10: At the end of the month, Circle Films pays its owners a ₹1,500 cash dividend. Cash and therefore assets decrease. Payments to a company's owners are dividends, which decrease retained earnings, so equity decreases. Table: Cash 9,750 -1,500 = 8,250; Retained Earnings 2,750 -1,500 = 1,250; total assets ₹27,250 = ₹11,000 + ₹16,250. Summary of Transactions: the ten transactions are summarized in Exhibit 3-2. Circle Films started the month with nothing but an idea and ended with ₹27,250 in assets, ₹11,000 in liabilities and ₹16,250 in equity. Changes to the left side of the equation equalled changes to the right side for all transactions, so the equation was always in balance. Every transaction affected at least two specific accounts: sometimes two asset accounts (#2 and #8), sometimes an asset and a liability account (#4 and #7), and sometimes an asset and an equity account (#1, #3, #5, #6, #9 and #10). Any combination affecting assets, liabilities and equity can occur, as long as the equation stays in balance. Exhibit 3-2 Transaction Summary for Circle Films: Cash +15,000, -10,000, +1,500, +2,000, -250, (none), (none), +3,500, -2,000, -1,500 totalling ₹8,250; Accounts Receivable +3,500 (#6) and -3,500 (#8) totalling ₹0; Supplies +1,000 (#2); Equipment +9,000 (#2) and +9,000 (#7) totalling ₹18,000; Unearned Revenue +2,000 (#4) giving ₹2,000; Notes Payable +9,000 (#7) giving ₹9,000; Common Stock +15,000 (#1); Retained Earnings +1,500 (#3), -250 (#5), +3,500 (#6), -2,000 (#9), -1,500 (#10) totalling ₹1,250. Totals: assets ₹27,250 = liabilities ₹11,000 + equity ₹16,250. Page 58.
